main_body: Altar block: a white upper panel carrying a purple banner with a gold cross, over a gold trim band and a purple front face with a second cross, on a grey stone base.
top_band: No distinct top surface. The column reads: light grey edge at rows 10-11, white with a purple cross banner at rows 11-23 (a vertical face), gold band at rows 24-25, brown line at row 25, then purple front at rows 26-35.
evidence: The only horizontal element is the 1-2 row gold trim with a brown line under it, which is a rim, not a surface. The large white area above it has a vertical cross banner painted on it, so it is a back panel seen face-on, not a lid seen from above. The purple front face has its cross and pleats painted flat with no inset. The result is two stacked front panels, which is a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The white block is a large flat fill of one colour with no grain or speckle. The purple front has only 2-3 tones with vertical stripes. The gold cross is a flat shape. There is no tinted outline and no material texture. The tiles carry few colours compared with the roofed stall and well references, which have roof tile highlights, wood grain and stone shading. It looks thinner and flatter than the references.
